summary: Siskiyou NF lookout in Curry County, Oregon: a 1947 L-4 cab on a 40-ft tower collapsed in winter 2007-08; sources say only the superstructure remains, and volunteers plan a reassembly.

facts.design: L-4 cab with catwalk on a 40-ft treated timber tower (1947); earlier L-4 on a 40-ft pole tower (1935)
facts.status_note: Cab collapsed under heavy snow in winter 2007-08; FireLookout.com (undated) says only the superstructure is standing

access.note: Road gated about 3/4 mile below the lookout and washed out in places above the gate; the Sand Mountain Society expects the lookout to be available through the Forest Service rental program once reassembled

corrections.why: The cab collapsed in winter 2007-08 and FireLookout.com says only the superstructure is standing; the record's standing status is not supported

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and FireLookout.com date the 40-ft L-4 tower to 1947; the Sand Mountain Society says snow crushed the lookout in 1946-47 and the present tower and cabin were built then. All three give 1947.

The register says occasionally staffed by the USFS or Coos FPA (undated); FireLookout.com says last staffed by Coos FPA in 1998. Recorded as unknown, because the sources disagree on whether anyone has staffed it since; the story reports both.
Register gives 3,644 ft (1,111 m); FireLookout.com gives 3778 ft; SMS gives 3,782 ft (1153 m). Record keeps the register's 1110.7 m; the sources differ by about 40 m.
FireLookout.com (undated) says only the superstructure is standing; the Sand Mountain Society project page describes planned reassembly. Not settled from the pages read.

notes_for_editor: Current condition is the main open question: FireLookout.com (undated) says only the superstructure stands; the SMS project page describes planned reassembly and may be out of date. A search summary mentioned a 2011 completion claim and earlier 1929 and 1931 cabins; I did not read those pages, so they are not used. The Oregon survey PDF (heritagedata load=34737) returned no extractable text. Access and gate claims rest on the SMS page only; check with the Gold Beach Ranger District. Fact-check 2026-10-08: staffing recorded as unknown (register and FireLookout.com disagree); fire-closure events retyped as other; story reworded where it went beyond the sources ("heavy snow", AWS post, "watching for aircraft"); Curry County and US 509, OR 101 evidence added.
